findings.problem: The two ~23-line proofs are the same argument: extensionality on a pair, `mem_graph_iff`, `mem_map`, then moving a witness `y` in each direction. They differ only in which scalar-action or negation lemma is used to unfold `(z • f) y` or `(-f) y`. Both theorems are really instances of one fact: post-composing a partial map with a linear endomorphism `φ` of `F` pushes its graph forward along `prodMap id φ`. Any further operation of this kind (for example `compPMap`) would need a third copy of the proof. A fix to one copy would have to be repeated in the other.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one general lemma, placed after `graph_map_snd_eq_range` and stated with `compPMap`, which already exists in the file:

theorem compPMap_graph (φ : F →ₗ[R] F) (f : E →ₗ.[R] F) :
    (φ.compPMap f).graph = f.graph.map ((LinearMap.id : E →ₗ[R] E).prodMap φ)

Proof sketch: `ext ⟨a, b⟩; simp only [mem_graph_iff, Submodule.mem_map, LinearMap.prodMap_apply, Prod.mk_inj, Prod.exists]`. Forward direction: from `y : f.domain` with `↑y = a` and `φ (f y) = b`, take the witness `(a, f y)`, which lies in `f.graph` via `y`. Backward direction: from `(a', b')` in `f.graph` via `y` with `a' = a` and `φ b' = b`, reuse `y`, using `compPMap_apply` for `(φ.compPMap f) y = φ (f y)`. The `compPMap` hypothesis is `RingHomCompTriple (RingHom.id R) (RingHom.id R) (RingHom.id R)`, which is available automatically.

Then rewrite the two theorems:

theorem smul_graph (f : E →ₗ.[R] F) (z : M) :
    (z • f).graph = f.graph.map ((LinearMap.id : E →ₗ[R] E).prodMap (z • (LinearMap.id : F →ₗ[R] F))) := by
  have : z • f = (z • (LinearMap.id : F →ₗ[R] F)).compPMap f := rfl  -- or `ext'` with `LinearMap.smul_comp`/`comp_id` if `rfl` fails
  rw [this, compPMap_graph]

theorem neg_graph (f : E →ₗ.[R] F) :
    (-f).graph = f.graph.map ((LinearMap.id : E →ₗ[R] E).prodMap (-(LinearMap.id : F →ₗ[R] F))) := by
  have : -f = (-(LinearMap.id : F →ₗ[R] F)).compPMap f := rfl  -- same fallback
  rw [this, compPMap_graph]

The hypotheses and statements of `smul_graph` and `neg_graph` stay exactly as they are.
findings.benefit: One 10-line graph-pushforward proof replaces two ~23-line copies, so the file gets shorter. The mathematical content is stated once, as a lemma that is also useful for other post-compositions. The two corollaries become short and make clear that `z • f` and `-f` are post-compositions with `z • id` and `-id`. A future change to `mem_graph_iff` or `prodMap` simp behaviour needs fixing in one place only.
